population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic for 2032→2034: of the 27.9 on in 2032, 58% stayed on (16.2). That is down from 60% because of bone-driven deprescribing in 65+ users, Bridge and Medicaid lockouts, and prices that stopped falling. The 11.7 who stopped joined the 9.1 already off, a pool of 20.8. Of those, 9.7 restarted (47%, down from 57%: 12-month waiver lockouts and the price stall slowed returns, and part of the return now runs through the gray market). That gives 16.2 + 9.7 = 25.9 on from the existing cohort. There were 3.0 pts of new ever-users, of whom 2.2 are on and 0.8 already off. On: 25.9 + 2.2 = 28.1. Ever: 37.0 + 3.0 = 40.0. Off: 20.8 − 9.7 + 0.8 = 11.9 = 40.0 − 28.1. Cycled: the 13.4 pts who had cycled by 2032, plus ~4.5 pts of first-time restarters and ~0.4 among new starters, give 18.3 of 40.0 = 46%. On ~270M adults: ≈75.9M on, ≈32.1M used and off, ≈162M never used. Age bands weighted 20/33/24/23%: 3.4 + 10.23 + 10.56 + 3.91 = 28.1. The 18–29 band rose 16→17 through the Army pre-accession track, AUD prescribing and gray retatrutide. The 65+ band is flat at 17 (≈10.6M): new dementia-label starts are offset by deprescribing after DEXA results and by Bridge non-responder cut-offs. Income thirds: (33.5 + 28.5 + 22.3)/3 = 28.1. The top third dipped slightly, from unmedicated chic in Brooklyn and Oakland and from users switching to the uncounted-in-share combination. The bottom third rose through HRSA AUD provision and $99–149 compounded product. The off-drug pool (≈32M) is now larger than the Medicare and Medicaid user counts combined. About a third of it was cut off by conditions rather than by choice, and a 2033 KFF survey puts 'stopped because of a bone scan or fracture' at ~9% of stoppers aged 65+. The ~162M never-users include an organised refuser constituency, the uninsured in non-expansion states, and people with contraindications. Pediatric: 1.3% of ~73M ≈ 950k, ~165k of them aged 6–11. The first children to start at 12 in 2023–24 are now adults.

access.public_coverage: The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge was renewed in Dec 2033 through Dec 2035 on unchanged terms: $225/month payment, $50 copay, and continuation tied to ≥5% loss by month 6, ≥80% PDC, and for 65+ an annual DEXA plus a resistance-training referral. Obesity users on the Bridge: ≈3.3M × $225 × 12 ≈ $8.9B/yr. Medicare overall pays 14.5% of fills ≈ 11.0M users (≈10.6M adults 65+ plus ~0.45M disabled under-65). Medicaid pays 11.5% ≈ 8.7M users × $225 × 12 ≈ $23.6B/yr combined federal and state. The same seven adherence-waiver states remain: Indiana, Arkansas, Missouri, Oklahoma, Georgia, Ohio and Montana. HRSA Community Incretin Access is flat-funded at $5.0B (FY2033 and FY2034 riders) and still unconditional. It serves ≈3.7M: 2.4M generic liraglutide × $70 × 12 = $2.0B, plus 1.32M semaglutide for cessation/AUD × $179 × 12 = $2.8B, ≈ $4.8B. TRICARE/VA/DoD cover ≈2.66M, including ~200k in the Metabolic Readiness Program (about 160k serving members and ~40k recruits who started on the pre-accession track): 200k × $149 × 12 ≈ $358M/yr. The tirzepatide/bimagrumab combination (Contura) is outside the Bridge's $225 bundle. Medicare covers it only through MA plan supplemental benefits, in a handful of plans.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 90+ semaglutide brands at $7–40/month, and generic tirzepatide is now sold in India, Brazil, Turkey, Mexico and Indonesia. Canada's generic semaglutide (~C$90–140/month) is the main legal-adjacent cross-border source for Americans under personal-importation tolerance. Chinese originator triple agonists (NMPA-approved) are exported across Asia and enter the US gray channel through Mexico and research-peptide resellers. US generic semaglutide entry dates under the patent settlements opened in 2033, but no ANDA had launched by end-2034 (see events). Tirzepatide remains protected to the mid-2030s.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Payer mix of ~75.9M users: commercial 37% (28.1M), Medicare 14.5% (11.0M), Medicaid 11.5% (8.7M), HRSA 4.9% (3.7M), TRICARE/VA/DoD 3.5% (2.66M), cash/direct 13.6% (10.3M), gray 15% (11.4M) = 100% (75.9M). Prices stalled. TrumpRx/direct stays at $249 semaglutide, $299 tirzepatide, $149 oral starts and $399 retatrutide for a third year, because the Strategic Supply Agreement's 2033 price review froze the ceilings through 2035 against Lilly's DPA plant debt and the expected generic semaglutide did not arrive. Wegovy list stays $1,349 and retatrutide list $1,499. The new Contura combination lists at $2,250, or $1,190 direct on allocation, with ~0.35M users, most of them commercial with prior authorisation and sarcopenia-risk criteria. Employer coverage is flat at 63%, but conditioned plans rose from ~55% to ~58% of covering employers, and two large PBMs pilot Bluetooth dose-logging pens as 'verified adherence' to counter skip-but-fill. Gray use grew from ~9.0M to ~11.4M through cash users priced out by the stall (direct-pay fell from 11.1M to 10.3M), lockout refugees from the waiver states and Bridge non-responders, and the Oct 2033 Fifth Circuit ruling that widened 503A 'personalised' compounding ($99–199). Gray product now includes compounded retatrutide and 'stack' kits with research-grade activin/myostatin agents sold as 'DIY Contura'.

GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus)
GLP-1 small-molecule, daily oral (orforglipron: Foundayo; BED low dose Jun 2032; AUD Apr 2034)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. US generics)
GLP-1 agonist / GIPR antagonist antibody-peptide conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide)

GIP/GLP-1 agonist plus activin type II receptor antibody, co-packaged weekly tirzepatide + monthly subcutaneous bimagrumab (Contura, Jul 2033)

alcohol use disorder (semaglutide injection, Jun 2030; orforglipron oral, Apr 2034; ASAM and VA/DoD guidelines list GLP-1 RAs as a first-line pharmacotherapy option, Sep 2033)

'brain health' semaglutide for 50–65-year-olds outside the dementia label

Contura requested by people under 50 with no sarcopenia risk as 'keep-the-frame' insurance; plans mostly deny it, which feeds the gray stack market
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The muscle-preserving next-gen driver is realised through the bimagrumab + tirzepatide BLA (filed Mar 2032), approved Jul 2033 after standard review. At 72 weeks it showed ~25% total loss with roughly 90% of it from fat versus ~70% on tirzepatide alone, and lean mass was preserved. There are no fracture, falls or functional-outcome data in 75+, and the label says so. Launch is antibody-capacity-limited (~0.35M users). Lilly markets it as 'Lose the weight. Keep the frame.' Amycretin got a second CRL in Sep 2033 on Novo fill-finish findings and was resubmitted in 2034, with a decision in 2035. MariTide supply expanded to ~1.4M users. Orforglipron AUD: sNDA filed Feb 2033 on a 52-week heavy-drinking-days trial, approved Apr 2034. No US generic semaglutide has launched. The 2033 settlement windows opened, but the two first-filer ANDAs received CRLs on peptide-related impurity and immunogenicity comparability, and a third filer's Indian API sits under FDA import alert and Section 232 duty. Global incretin market ≈$172B in 2034. US volume grew ~2%, US net price is flat, and global growth is ex-US volume at generic prices.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Rates are elevated with retatrutide 12 mg, gray product without titration, and Contura (diarrhoea from the bimagrumab component).

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and intestinal obstruction (mass tort)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: MDL 3094 has ~74,000 filed and tolled claims. Two more bellwethers split, and Novo and Lilly announced a partial inventory settlement for ileus claims (2034). Persistent-gastroparesis claims are still contested.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Ileus labelled. FDA still declines to label persistent gastroparesis.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Absolute cases rise with retatrutide 12 mg and rapid loss.
Registries still show low absolute risk. The AUD indication adds a population with high baseline pancreatitis risk, which muddies the signal further.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; the orforglipron AUD label carries a precaution for active heavy drinkers with prior pancreatitis.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: NHANES-DXA 2031–33 confirms the 2029–31 pattern: appendicular lean mass ~0.5 SD lower in 65+ users more than 2 years on drug, with sarcopenia criteria met at ~1.6×. The gap is smaller where Bridge training referrals were actually used (~40% uptake). Worst on liraglutide and compounded product.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings retained. Contura approved on lean-mass data. Bridge training referral retained. HRSA still has no requirement, and the HELP letter is unanswered.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Medicare hip-fracture admissions rose another ~3% in 2032–33. Modelled excess ≈ 10.6M users 65+ × ~0.5%/yr × HR 0.35 ≈ 18,500 hip fractures/yr, concentrated in women and cyclers, with partial offset where antiresorptive cover is used. The final adjudicated adolescent registry (Nov 2033) shows lumbar-spine BMD accrual ~0.15 SD lower after adjustment for weight loss, with no excess fractures yet.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric labelling updated in Mar 2034: baseline and 2-year DEXA for adolescents on drug more than 2 years, with no restriction. DEXA for 65+ remains in Warnings (not boxed). AACE/Endocrine Society bone-cover guidance retained.

safety_ledger.effect: Atypical femoral fracture and osteonecrosis of the jaw from long-term 'bone cover'
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Antiresorptive co-prescription now covers ~3M incretin users, some under 65 and on continuous bisphosphonates beyond 5 years. Early case series of atypical femoral fractures and rebound vertebral fractures after stopping denosumab appear in cyclers who drop both drugs at once.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: ASBMR advisory on drug-holiday sequencing (2034); no FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Training stress fractures in drug-assisted recruits
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: TRADOC data from Fort Jackson and Fort Sill (2034): lower-extremity stress-fracture rates in basic training ~1.5× higher among recruits who entered via the pre-accession incretin track than among matched non-users. Confounding by prior fitness is unresolved.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Army adds a 30-day protein and loading phase and a calcium/vitamin D protocol; DoD Inspector General review requested by the House Armed Services Committee.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still conflicting cohorts; very low absolute risk.
No causal association, including in the BED and AUD populations.

Long-term-user surveys hold at ~10–15% reduced pleasure. The share reporting at least one deliberate dose holiday in the past year rose to ~50%. The orforglipron AUD trial reported anhedonia scores in ~5% versus ~3% on placebo.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Retatrutide Adverse Reactions entry and class precaution above maintenance doses retained. FTC continues to police non-manufacturer 'calm' claims.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Driven by conditioning cut-offs and now by bone-related deprescribing in 65+. The off pool is ≈32M adults.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Indiana and Arkansas waiver challenge unresolved; no federal rule.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Protein, iron, B12 and vitamin D signals persist. Thiamine deficiency is flagged in AUD users eating very little.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance. The orforglipron AUD label recommends thiamine assessment.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon, adolescent, pediatric and cycling effects
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of adult and eleven years of adolescent follow-up. ~165k children aged 6–11 are on drug. Pubertal-timing data are still absent.

Poison-centre incretin calls rose ~20% from 2032 with the gray resurgence. New categories: injection-site abscesses and hypersensitivity from research-grade 'bimagrumab' and activin-ligand products, which independent testing found mostly mislabelled, and dosing errors with compounded retatrutide.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA import alert on research-grade antibodies marketed for human use (2034). Second federal indictment of a distributor. The Fifth Circuit's 503A ruling limits FDA action against 'personalised' compounders.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg.
'Brain health' prescribing in 50–64-year-olds outside the label continues, now partly redirected to Contura by affluent patients who want the frame protected.

safety_ledger.effect: Bimagrumab-combination effects (muscle spasm, diarrhoea, acne, raised liver enzymes)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Muscle spasm ~20% early in the trials, mostly transient. Long-term bone effects of activin-receptor blockade with incretin-driven weight loss are unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled. Postmarketing requirement for a fracture and falls study in 65+, due 2038.

food_and_beverage.state: With adoption flat at ~28%, the shock has become a baseline: US packaged-food volume falls ~1.5–2% a year rather than 2.5%. Snack divestitures continue at lower multiples. 'Bone-and-muscle' protein formats grow, and Contura's 'keep the frame' campaign is co-marketed with whey makers. Hormel and Tyson pitch lean-protein supply to the Army pre-accession programme.

alcohol.state: A fifth straight year of falling US spirits and beer volume. An oral AUD option, a guideline endorsement and VA/DoD use have moved incretins into mainstream addiction care. Kentucky bourbon warehouses report record aged inventory. Distillers push exports, non-alcoholic lines and 'holiday weekend' packs timed to dose breaks.

restaurants.state: Unit closures in value chains slow but continue. Restaurants near Fort Sill and Fort Bragg report smaller checks. Church-hall 'Open Table' suppers grow into a national network but remain commercially invisible. Bars in college towns report the steepest weekday declines.

apparel.state: Size ranges remain wide because the cycling population moves between sizes. Uniform suppliers re-cut again for pre-accession recruits. Hip protectors and fall-safe footwear are standard senior catalogue lines.

fitness.state: Prescribed resistance training keeps growing through Bridge referrals, employer conditions and Medicare Advantage strength benefits. Contura's marketing pitches the drug as a substitute for the gym, so low-cost gym chains run 'muscle you earn' counter-ads. The gray stack trade revives inside gyms.

insurance.state: Pharmacy trend slows to ~+6% as volume flattens and net prices freeze. Plans hold the line through conditions, Contura prior authorisation and dose-logging pen pilots. The wellness-differential cases split, with the Sixth Circuit upholding and the Ninth vacating, and a certiorari petition is pending.

pharma.state: US incretin revenue plateaus: flat net price, ~2% volume growth, and a growing gray share. Lilly grows on Contura and ex-US exports. Novo shrinks in the US after the amycretin CRL and its tariff burden. Generic filers absorb CRL costs. Chinese originators gain global share. MDL inventory settlement reserves are booked.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: The compliant body now has a further tier. Lean, muscled and DEXA-documented reads as Bridge-renewed and employer-qualified, and a body that is lean without visible softness reads as Contura money. 'Pen-thin' signals ordinary coverage without coaching, and a soft, heavier body reads as cut off, priced out or refusing. Military haircuts on thin, fragile-looking teenagers at Fort Sill have become a recognised image.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Price stopped falling, so the class gradient stopped narrowing. The affluent buy frame-preservation: Contura, trainers and bone cover. The middle buys $299 tirzepatide or goes gray. The locked-out buy $99 vials from 'personalised' compounders. In Sun City, Arizona, gyms that had waiting lists now also hold 'bone club' sessions where women compare T-scores.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Open Table spread from Grand Rapids, Nashville and Tulsa into ~1,400 congregations and now runs regular suppers near Fort Sill and Fort Bragg for military families. The Southern Baptist Convention's 2033 resolution on 'appetite stewardship' opposes coercive conditioning but not the drug itself, and many attenders are on drug. Oakland's fat-liberation 'Unmedicated' supper clubs host a national gathering. Family tables where one parent is on, one is off and a teenager is on an adolescent dose are ordinary.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles list the molecule, and some add 'frame-protected' or 'unmedicated since 2029'. Dose holidays are negotiated around conditioned-plan windows and now around dose-logging pens, which make a skipped injection visible to the PBM.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Clinical, contractual and, for the backlash, sacred. 'Appetite liberty' laws now cover four states: Kentucky and Utah joined Tennessee and Idaho in 2034. In AA rooms the argument is whether a pen counts as sobriety, and many groups now say 'it counts if you come'.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. ~10–15% of long-term users report reduced pleasure, and ~8% meet clinically meaningful anhedonia criteria at high retatrutide doses. Deliberate dose holidays in the past year rose to ~50% of long-term users. Skip-but-fill persists, and dose-logging pen pilots (~1.5M enrollees) make it detectable for the first time. Foundayo low dose for BED and off-label 'quiet' use reached ~1.4M. Foundayo for AUD reached ~0.6M by end-2034 inside the commercial, VA and cash shares, and HRSA serves AUD and cessation through semaglutide.
interior_life.framing: Still a complaint and a treatment. 'The grey' is ordinary vocabulary. For AUD patients the same effect is described as relief: 'the craving went quiet and so did some other things.' Clinicians say 'reward modulation'. Backlash pastors say 'chemical contentment'. Recovery counsellors argue about whether flattened pleasure is a cost or the point.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Sales staff still time holidays to quarter-end. Dose-logging pens in two PBM pilots mean conditioned-plan employees can no longer skip quietly, and the first union grievance (UAW, Ohio) frames the pen as workplace surveillance. Army chaplains report recruits on the pre-accession track describing 'the grey' and homesickness in the same breath. Police unions bargain over drug-holiday leave around fitness tests.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off-dose' billing is standard. Festivals keep 'holiday weekend' passes. A cycle of stand-up specials about the dose-logging pen is the year's comedy trend. Sports-betting handle growth stays below pre-2028 trend, and casinos cite it in earnings calls.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Holidays around anniversaries and conception remain routine. Couples on logged pens must choose between a recorded skip and an uncomfortable weekend. Sex therapists cite both the retatrutide label and the Contura label, whose spasm and fatigue entries are mentioned on dates.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Same cross-party blocs. Pro-access populists defend frozen TrumpRx prices and the readiness programme as patriotic. The backlash coalition of anti-pharma groups, religious conservatives and fat liberation now has state laws, a Baptist resolution and ~5,200 military religious-accommodation requests. The 2034 midterm question shifted from 'are you on?' to 'would you let the Army put your son on it?'

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access, price-freezing and label-not-restrict. Approves new forms and indications (Contura, oral AUD) and manages bone and muscle risk through labelling and postmarketing requirements. Holds generic semaglutide to strict peptide comparability standards, which delays entry and suits the national-champion bargain. Enforcement against the gray market is hampered by the Fifth Circuit 503A ruling and falls on importers and distributors, not users.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate to take the drug. Medicare Bridge renewed unchanged through 2035. HRSA flat at $5.0B and unconditional. The DoD Metabolic Readiness Program has expanded to a pre-accession track. The ACA cessation mandate is unchanged. The Strategic Supply Agreement price review froze federal ceiling prices through 2035.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Conditioning is entrenched but not extended in law: seven Medicaid waivers, Bridge continuation rules, and employer outcomes-based plans (~58% of covering employers). The new layer is technical: PBM dose-logging pen pilots. Four states ban premium conditioning. The circuit split on wellness differentials awaits the Supreme Court.
state.workforce_or_military: The Army's Future Soldier Metabolic Track (May 2033) lets applicants up to 6 points over body-fat standards ship after 90 days on tirzepatide supplied by DoD. About 40k recruits entered by end-2034, and ~200k service members and recruits are on drug in the readiness programme. Body-composition separations are down ~40% from the 2030 baseline. Stress-fracture data at Fort Jackson and Fort Sill prompted a loading-phase protocol. VA and DoD added AUD treatment with semaglutide or Foundayo to substance-use programmes. About 5,200 religious-accommodation requests have been filed. Police and fire contracts in Phoenix, Houston and Chicago continue, Dallas and Atlanta have added them, and CBP and federal wildland fire crews were added in 2034.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Section 232 duties on incretin API remain. The Lilly national-champion terms were extended in exchange for frozen ceilings. India's WTO consultation became a panel request (2033) and is unresolved, while Indian generics supply most of the Global South and, through Canada and Mexico, part of the US gray channel. Chinese amino-acid export controls continue, and Chinese triple agonists reach US gray buyers through research resellers. Novo still pays duty on Danish API.

events.event: The first settlement window for US generic semaglutide opens with no product on shelves. FDA issues complete response letters to the two first filers over peptide-impurity and immunogenicity comparability, and a third filer's Indian API remains under import alert. Weeks later Commerce's review of the Strategic Supply Agreement freezes TrumpRx ceilings at $249, $299, $149 and $399 through 2035.

The Army launches a Future Soldier Metabolic Track. Applicants up to six points over body-fat standards may ship to basic training after 90 days on DoD-supplied tirzepatide. Religious-accommodation requests climb past 4,000, and the Southern Baptist Convention adopts an 'appetite stewardship' resolution opposing coercive conditioning.

FDA approves Lilly's Contura, weekly tirzepatide co-packaged with monthly bimagrumab, on data showing about 90% of weight lost came from fat. It lists at $2,250 a month ($1,190 direct, allocated) with the tagline 'Lose the weight. Keep the frame'. The label notes there are no fracture or falls data.

The Fifth Circuit rules that FDA's 'essentially a copy' guidance cannot bar 503A pharmacies from 'personalised' incretin preparations with a documented clinical rationale. Telehealth compounders scale compounded retatrutide and 'frame stack' kits, and gray users pass 11 million by 2034.

Congress renews the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge through 2035 on unchanged terms ($225 payment, $50 copay, 5%/80%/DEXA conditions) after hearings on CMS data showing a second year of rising hip-fracture admissions. HRSA's incretin programme is renewed flat at $5.0B.

FDA approves orforglipron (Foundayo) as the first oral incretin for alcohol use disorder, following ASAM and VA/DoD guidelines that list GLP-1 drugs as a first-line option. VA and DoD fold it into substance-use programmes.

open_tensions: Contura is sold as having solved 'skinny-frail', but it has no fracture or falls data. The Bridge's $225 bundle excludes it, so older Americans with the highest fracture risk mostly get tirzepatide plus a bisphosphonate while affluent 50-year-olds get the frame-protecting combination. The postmarketing fracture study reports in 2038 and the Bridge expires in Dec 2025+10, at the end of 2035.

Dose-logging pens can expose skip-but-fill just as ~50% of long-term users take deliberate holidays for 'the grey'. If the Supreme Court takes the wellness-differential circuit split, it will decide whether a logged skipped injection can raise someone's premium, and the UAW grievance tests the same question in bargaining.

Frozen prices and stalled generic entry rest on FDA comparability rulings and the national-champion deal. A cleared ANDA, an adverse WTO panel or Lilly's DPA debt terms could break the price freeze before 2035, while the Fifth Circuit's 503A ruling has already moved 15% of users outside any regulator's view, including into mislabelled research antibodies.

The Army's pre-accession track fills ranks and lowers separations, but recruits who entered through it fracture more often in basic training. Congress must decide in FY2035 whether to expand it to the Navy and Marines while the IG review and 5,200 accommodation requests are pending and four states legislate 'appetite liberty'.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is sold in the US.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
TrumpRx/direct prices remain $249 for semaglutide injection, $299 for tirzepatide, $149 for oral starting doses and $399 for retatrutide.

Indiana's and Arkansas's 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins with a 12-month lockout after two misses, and the disability-rights challenge is still unresolved.
The ACA preventive mandate still requires plans to cover semaglutide for smoking cessation in two 90-day courses a year.

prose.headline: Seventy-Six Million and Holding: The Pen Stopped Getting Cheaper, and the Army Started Shipping Thin Recruits
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034 the share of American adults on an incretin drug has barely moved in two years. It is just over twenty-eight percent, about seventy-six million people. Underneath the flat number there is constant movement. Forty percent of adults have now used one of these drugs. About thirty-two million have stopped, and nearly half of everyone who ever started has quit and come back at least once. A third of those who stopped did not choose to. They missed a weigh-in in Oklahoma, failed to lose five percent by month six on the Medicare Bridge, or got a bone scan result their doctor did not like.

The price stopped falling. Generic semaglutide was supposed to arrive in 2033, and the settlement dates came and went. The FDA rejected the first two applications over impurity data, and the third depends on Indian ingredients held at the border. A few weeks later the Commerce Department froze the federal ceiling prices, $249, $299, $149 and $399, through 2035, citing the loans behind Lilly's new plants. Congress renewed the Medicare Bridge on the same terms as before, and community health centres still hand out free liraglutide with no questions asked. Nobody's coverage changed. Prices simply stayed where they were.

When the legal price stays put, buyers find other sources. In October 2033 a federal appeals court ruled that compounding pharmacies may make 'personalised' versions of the drugs if a prescriber documents a reason. Telehealth sites now sell compounded retatrutide for ninety-nine dollars. Canadian generic semaglutide crosses the border in luggage. More than eleven million Americans now buy outside regulated channels, about one user in seven. The newest gray product is the frame stack, a vial sold as a muscle-preserving antibody. Independent labs find that most of these vials contain something else.

The frame stack copies something real. In July 2033 Lilly launched Contura, tirzepatide packaged with a monthly antibody that keeps muscle on while fat comes off. The tagline is 'Lose the weight. Keep the frame.' It costs $2,250 a month at list. Medicare's $225 bundle does not cover it, and its label states that no one has measured whether it prevents broken bones. Hip-fracture admissions have risen for a second year. The final adolescent registry found slower bone growth in teenagers on the drugs, though no excess fractures yet. In Sun City, Arizona, women swap bone-density scores at the gym.

The state is still the steadiest customer. Since May 2033 the Army has let applicants who are over its body-fat limit enlist after ninety days on tirzepatide. Forty thousand have done so. At Fort Sill and Fort Jackson, recruits who came in that way get stress fractures half again as often as others, and the Army has added a protein phase to training. The VA now prescribes the new oral pill approved in April for alcohol use disorder. In Louisville the warehouses are full of bourbon that is not selling.

The flatness people call 'the grey' is still the country's main complaint about the drugs. Half of long-term users take deliberate breaks. Two pharmacy-benefit managers are testing pens that report each injection, so a skipped dose shows up in a file, and the auto workers' union in Ohio has filed a grievance calling it surveillance. People treated for drinking describe the same flatness as relief.

The backlash has become organised. Open Table suppers now run in about fourteen hundred churches, including outside Army posts. The Southern Baptists passed a resolution against coercive conditions without condemning the drug itself. Four states bar employers from tying premiums to it. Oakland's unmedicated supper clubs held a national gathering. From the outside the country looks lean, sober and steady. Inside, people are tracked and fragile, and the prices are frozen.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Rhonda Pickett clocks in at the Reasor's deli in Tulsa at six and slices honey ham for people who will eat two pieces. She has worked out who is on by how thin they ask for it.

Her SoonerCare got locked in March. She missed two weigh-ins while her mother was in hospice, and the lockout runs twelve months. Now a telehealth pharmacy in Texas mails her a vial labelled 'semaglutide, personalised, with B12' for $129, and she draws it up with an insulin syringe on the bathroom counter. The vial is pinkish. The old pens were not.

At lunch she reads a text from Tyler at Fort Sill: 'Shins hurt. They gave us chalk milk. Love u.' He shipped in August, eleven pounds over, after ninety days on what the recruiter called 'the readiness shot'. He sent a photo of his new haircut, and his collarbones looked like someone else's.

After work she drives to First Methodist for Open Table. Pastor Dale sets out a full plate of brisket, beans, cornbread and peach cobbler and says the line about hunger and how we were made. Rhonda eats half. Nobody comments. Ginny, two seats down, is on the Bridge and talks about her T-score the way other women talk about grandchildren.

Walking out, Rhonda counts. Five more months on the lockout, two more vials, then a weigh-in she will have to pass on day one.

At home she skips tonight's dose. She wants to taste the cobbler again tomorrow, cold, standing at the fridge. There is no pen to log it.
